title: Minkowski inequality for finite sums
statement: Let $I,K$ be sets, let $r\in\bbr$ with $1\le r$, and let $s\subseteq I$ and $t\subseteq K$ be finite. Suppose $a:I\times K\to\bbr$ satisfies $a(i,j)\ge0$ for every $i\in s$ and $j\in t$. Then $\displaystyle\left(\sum_{j\in t}\left(\sum_{i\in s}a(i,j)\right)^r\right)^{1/r}\le\sum_{i\in s}\left(\sum_{j\in t}a(i,j)^r\right)^{1/r}$.
replaced: Let $s\subseteq I$ and $t\subseteq J$ be finite sets, let $r\ge1$, and let $a:I\times J\to\bbr$ satisfy $a(i,j)\ge0$ for $i\in s$, $j\in t$. Then $(\sum_{j\in t}(\sum_{i\in s}a(i,j))^r)^{1/r}\le\sum_{i\in s}(\sum_{j\in t}a(i,j)^r)^{1/r}$.
